intro: You're looking for haulage insurance because you run lorries, vans or a haulage operation and need cover that fits the reality of the road. Whether you're renewing, switching broker or insuring a new vehicle, finding someone local who understands goods in transit, O-licences and driver history makes the conversation easier. iComply introduces you to a UK insurance broker who can quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for haulage insurance near me usually need
need_lead: Most people searching this phrase want a broker who can arrange cover for their vehicles, loads and liabilities without guesswork.
needs: You operate HGVs or a mixed fleet and need cover that matches your O-licence obligations.
You carry other people's goods and need goods in transit cover as a separate arrangement from vehicle insurance.
You employ or use drivers with varied histories and need a broker who will look at the detail rather than decline outright.
You are starting out or expanding and need to insure a new vehicle or additional driver quickly.
You want to speak to someone local who understands haulage and can explain what is and is not included.
context_heading: Why local knowledge matters for haulage cover
context: Haulage insurance is not one product. Vehicle cover, goods in transit and liability for haulage operators are usually arranged separately, and a broker should talk through each part with you. If you hold an O-licence, you need cover that meets the conditions attached to it, so it is worth being clear about your licence and operations from the start.

Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm. You can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association (BIBA), and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute. A broker must understand your demands and needs, explain key policy features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: The type of vehicles you run, such as HGVs, vans or a mixed fleet, and what they are used for.
Whether you hold an O-licence and the kind of work you do, for example general haulage or carrying specific goods.
Whether you need goods in transit cover and the typical value of loads you carry.
The driving history of anyone who will be driving, including any points, convictions or claims.
Your current cover and renewal date, if you have one, so the broker can compare like for like.
Any particular requirements, such as cover for European journeys or for subcontractors.
questions: Will the policy cover my O-licence obligations and what evidence will I need to provide?
Is goods in transit cover included or separate, and what limits apply?
How will my drivers' histories affect the quote and what details do you need from me?
What are the key exclusions I should know about for haulage work?
How are you paid for arranging this cover and will that be explained in writing?
If I need to make a claim, what is the process and who handles it?

faqs.q: Do I need separate goods in transit cover if I already have vehicle insurance?
faqs.a: Yes, goods in transit cover is usually separate from vehicle insurance. Vehicle insurance typically covers the vehicle itself and third-party liabilities, while goods in transit covers the loads you carry. A broker can confirm what your existing policy includes.

faqs.q: What is an O-licence and why does it matter for insurance?
faqs.a: An O-licence is the operator licence required for goods vehicles over a certain weight. Insurers need to know you hold one because cover must meet the conditions attached to it. A broker will ask about your licence when arranging haulage insurance.

faqs.q: Will my drivers' history affect the quote?
faqs.a: Yes, driver history matters for haulage insurance. Points, convictions and claims can affect the premium and the terms offered. It helps to have details of all drivers ready when you speak to a broker.

faqs.q: How do I check that a broker is properly authorised?
faqs.a: You can check on the FCA register to see if a broker is authorised or is an appointed representative of an authorised firm. Many brokers also belong to BIBA, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

extra_heading: Choosing between local brokers for haulage cover
extra: Searching for haulage insurance near me suggests you would rather deal with someone you could actually sit down with, especially when your operation is not straightforward. A nearby broker can visit your yard, look over your vehicles and talk through your routes and loads in person, which often makes it easier to explain the detail that affects a haulage quote.

When you compare brokers, ask what they specialise in rather than assuming all cover is the same. Some deal mainly with private cars, while others handle fleets, goods in transit and operator licence conditions as a matter of course. Ask how many haulage clients they look after and whether they place cover with insurers who understand your type of work, then judge for yourself which broker fits.

It also helps to ask how each broker is paid and whether they charge a fee as well as commission, so you can weigh up the overall cost rather than just the headline premium. Check each one on the FCA register before you commit, and ask whether they belong to BIBA or hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute if that matters to you. A short conversation usually tells you whether they understand haulage or are simply quoting from a standard form.

extra_faqs.q: Is it better to use a local haulage insurance broker than one further away?
extra_faqs.a: A local broker can visit your premises, see your vehicles and discuss your operation face to face, which can be helpful for complex haulage risks. Distance alone does not decide quality, though, so weigh up their haulage experience and how clearly they explain cover alongside how near they are.

extra_faqs.q: What should I have ready before I speak to a broker about haulage cover?
extra_faqs.a: Have details of your vehicles, your O-licence, the goods you carry and the driving histories of everyone who will be driving. It also helps to know your current cover and renewal date so the broker can compare like for like. The more you can tell them up front, the more useful the first conversation will be.
